title: A birational dimension-one local overring of a nonfield Noetherian local domain
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a nonzero local integral domain, with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B\ne0$. Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] containing $B$, with every element of $K$ expressible as $b/c$ for $b,c\in B$ and $c\ne0$. There exists a subring $R\subseteq K$ containing $B$ which is a Noetherian local integral domain of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$ satisfying $\mathfrak m_R\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$. The fraction field of $R$, with the given embedding, is $K$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, algebra-lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, clauses (1) and (2); the same-fraction-field clause follows from the inclusions B ⊆ R ⊆ K in its statement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-domain-proper-principal-chart] to $B\subseteq K$. It gives nonzero generators $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ of $\mathfrak m_B$, a selected generator $a$, and the Noetherian subring $S=B[x_1/a,\ldots,x_r/a]\subseteq K$ with $\mathfrak m_BS=aS\ne S$. The inclusion in the field makes $S$ a nonzero integral domain.

source.place: Tag 00P8, algebra-lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof from choosing a dominating valuation ring through S contained in A and x_r S not equal to S (original item steps 1-3 and properness part of step 4).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-principalized-maximal-ideal-height-one-prime] to $B\subseteq S$ and $a$. All its hypotheses were obtained in step 1. Choose the resulting prime $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $aS$ with $\operatorname{ht}_S(\mathfrak q)=1$ and $\mathfrak q\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, algebra-lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof sentences choosing a minimal prime over x_r S, proving height one, and proving that it lies over the original maximal ideal (original item steps 4-5).

proof.text: Define the required ring as the actual subring $R=\{s/t\in K:s\in S,\ t\in S\setminus\mathfrak q\}$. The complement of the prime $\mathfrak q$ is multiplicative and excludes zero, so field addition and multiplication show this is a subring containing $S$. The fraction construction of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] identifies it with $S_{\mathfrak q}$: equality of fractions in $K$ is $s t'=s' t$, exactly the localization equality because $S$ is a domain. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak n=\{s/t:s\in\mathfrak q,\ t\notin\mathfrak q\}$. Numerator membership in $\mathfrak q$ is independent of presentation by cross multiplication and primality. This set is a proper ideal, while a fraction outside it has inverse $t/s\in R$; hence it is the unique maximal ideal. The inclusion in $K$ makes $R$ a nonzero integral domain.

source.place: Tag 00P8, lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, final sentence R prime = S_q; Tag 00CO, definition-localization

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to $S\to R$: all $t\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ have inverses $1/t$, every element is $s/t$, and injectivity gives its kernel condition (take multiplier $1$). Thus $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], its Krull dimension equals $\operatorname{ht}_S(\mathfrak q)=1$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, conclusion; Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Tag 00KF, definition-height

proof.text: For $b\in B$, the fraction $b/1$ belongs to $\mathfrak n$ exactly when $b\in\mathfrak q$, and this is equivalent to $b\in\mathfrak m_B$. Thus $\mathfrak m_R\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$. Finally the embedding of $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ into $K$ sends $r/s$ to the same field quotient. It is injective because equality is cross multiplication in the domain $R$. It is surjective because every $k\in K$ has the form $b/c$ with $b,c\in B\subseteq R$ and $c\ne0$. This proves the asserted equality of fraction fields with the prescribed embedding.

source.place: Tag 00P8, lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, clause (2) and the inclusions in the statement

proof_origin.place: Tag 00P8, lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof; the principal-height bound is specialized from the existing Tag 00KW height-quotient node and the same-field clause is expanded explicitly.
